# 0014. The draw sequence is generated by arithmetic written in this repository, and no crate supplies it

## Status

Accepted.

## Date

2026-08-09.

## The question

`0004-uncertainty-model.md` decided that uncertainty is carried by sampling
throughout, with no analytic path. Every reported region therefore rests on a
population of draws, and where those draws come from is the difference between a
reconstruction a second party can repeat and one they cannot.

`0009-determinism.md` already fixed the property. It requires that every sampling
draw come from one explicitly seeded generator whose algorithm is fixed by this
project and not taken from a platform default, so that the sequence of numbers is
identical everywhere, and it requires that reductions over samples run in a fixed
order. What it did not fix is where that generator comes from, and the answer is
not obvious: the language taken in `0002-language-and-toolchain.md` has no
generator in its standard library, so something has to supply one.

`0002-language-and-toolchain.md` named `rand` as a candidate crate and decided
none of the candidates. `../DEPENDENCIES.md` records that this question is taken
here rather than there. This record takes it.

## The options considered

**Take a crate and use whatever generator it offers by default.** Shortest to
write and the ordinary thing to do. Cost: the sequence is then fixed by that
crate's choice of default rather than by anything in this tree, and a default is
the part of a library most likely to be improved. The promise in 0009 would rest
on a version requirement in a manifest.

**Take a crate and name a generator inside it whose algorithm is documented as
stable.** Better, and the honest comparison for this record. Cost: a dependency
and its graph, an entry in `../DEPENDENCIES.md` against the ceiling stated there,
a name in the allowed list in `crates/einschlag/tests/nothing_goes_out.rs`, and a
version pin to maintain, all for an amount of arithmetic that fits on a page. The
algorithm is still fixed somewhere other than this tree, so reading what the tool
actually does means reading a crate at a version rather than reading a file.

What either crate guarantees about the stability of its sequence was not read at
a commit in this tree and is not quoted here. The comparison above does not rest
on it: the cost side is what decides, and it is the same cost whatever the
guarantee says.

**Write the arithmetic here.** The state advance and the seeding are a few lines
each, they have no dependencies, and the file is the authority for what the tool
does. Cost: this project owns a numerical component forever and has to test it,
and a mistake in it is invisible in a way most mistakes are not, because a
sequence that is subtly wrong looks exactly as unpatterned as one that is right.

**Draw from the platform's entropy source at the point of use.** Listed so that
the list is not a rationalisation. It has no seed, so a run cannot be repeated,
which 0009 refuses outright.

## The option taken

**The arithmetic is written in this repository, in
`crates/einschlag/src/sampling.rs`, and nothing else in the library produces a
draw.**

Precisely, so that a reader can tell whether a piece of code complies:

- A generator is constructed from an integer seed and from nothing else. It
  reads no clock, no environment and no platform entropy source, and neither does
  anything else in the library.
- The state is 256 bits, advanced by a xor, shift and rotate construction, and
  the seed is expanded into that state by a multiply, shift and xor mixer. The
  shape is a published one. This record does not cite an edition of it, because
  none was read at this commit, and the tree does not depend on the name: what it
  depends on is the arithmetic written out in that file, pinned by a test that
  refuses a change to the produced sequence.
- The two distributions `0004-uncertainty-model.md` reads the stated input forms
  as, a normal and a uniform over a closed interval, are derived from that one
  sequence and from no other.
- Reductions over a population run in index order, in one thread.
- A check refuses a source of draws or of entropy anywhere else in the workspace,
  by name, in `crates/einschlag/tests/one_seeded_generator.rs`.

## The reasons

**The cost of a crate here is paid in the wrong currency.** A dependency is worth
taking where it supplies something this project could not write well, which is
the argument `0013-platform-math-out-of-the-numeric-core.md` made for the
transcendental implementation: correctly rounded elementary functions are a
numerical-methods project. A generator is not that. It is a fixed sequence of
integer operations with no accuracy question in it, and the reason to import one
would be convenience rather than competence.

**The property 0009 asks for is stronger when the algorithm is in the tree.** The
sentence in that record is that the algorithm is fixed by this project. A pinned
crate satisfies the letter of it and puts the thing being relied on one step away
from the reader, behind a version requirement and a lock file the repository does
not yet track. A file in the tree is read at the commit that depends on it, which
is the same argument `README.md` in this directory makes for records themselves.

**The invisibility of a mistake is the real cost and it is answered directly
rather than argued away.** A wrong sequence looks right. What answers it is not
confidence in the arithmetic but a test that pins the produced values, so that
any change to the construction, including a correction, has to be a deliberate
one that a reader sees.

## What this costs

**This project now owns a component whose statistical quality it has not
established.** No test suite for generators was run against this implementation
and none is quoted anywhere in the tree. What is established is that the sequence
is reproducible and that it is pinned. Whether it is a good source of draws for
tail behaviour at the levels the regions in #44 will be reported at is not
established here, and #50 is where a coverage figure would show it if it were
not.

**A correction to the arithmetic changes every reported region.** The pinned test
makes that visible rather than silent, and it also means a fix is a change with a
version consequence, which `0009-determinism.md` already says a reader has to be
told about in release notes.

**The name is a description rather than an attestation.** A reader who wants to
know that this is a particular published generator cannot learn it from this
record, because no published test vector was compared against. The cost falls on
a reader who would have taken the name as a warrant, and the way not to pay it is
to read the file.

**Nobody gets the surrounding library.** A crate would have brought distributions,
weighted choice and shuffling. Anything of that kind this project needs later has
to be written here, and each addition is another piece of arithmetic to test.

## What would falsify this

**A coverage figure from #50 that is wrong in a way that tracks the generator
rather than the model.** Regions stated at a level should contain the truth at
about that rate; if they do not, and the same computation driven by a different
sequence behaves differently, the fault is here.

**A statistical test suite failing against this implementation.** That would be
the direct measurement this record admits it does not have.

**A distribution this project needs turning out to be hard.** The reasoning above
rests on the arithmetic being small. If sampling from something the model
requires becomes a numerical-methods problem in its own right, the comparison
this record made no longer holds and the crate option returns with a different
answer.

**The sample counts the regions need turning out to be large enough for the
generator's speed to matter.** No run time was measured here, and
`0004-uncertainty-model.md` already names run time on ordinary hardware as a
thing that could falsify a decision of its own.

## Evidence

The requirement that every draw come from one explicitly seeded generator whose
algorithm is fixed by this project, and that reductions run in a fixed order, is
quoted from `0009-determinism.md` in this directory.

The candidate list this record takes one question out of is in
`0002-language-and-toolchain.md`, and `../DEPENDENCIES.md` records which issue
takes which candidate.

No number in this record was measured. There is no run time, no sample count and
no statistical result in it, because none has been produced.
